channel.title: Qilich blog
channel.description: For business owners: prices, timelines, decisions.

item.title: What to automate first in a small business
item.description: Where to start with automation: find the repetitive work, rank it by cost and risk, and don’t pay for software where a spreadsheet will do.

item.title: Will automation pay for itself? A simple way to calculate it
item.description: When the money spent on software or a bot comes back: how to count hours saved, fewer errors, orders not lost, and the running costs.

item.title: Telegram bot cost in Tashkent: what drives the price
item.description: From a menu bot to one with payments, CRM sync and AI: what really sets the price of a Telegram bot, where you can save and where you shouldn’t.

item.title: What a mobile app costs in Tashkent: where the budget goes
item.description: What sets the price of an iOS and Android app: user journeys, backend, payments, integrations, store publishing, and the costs that start after launch.

item.title: Website cost in Tashkent: from landing page to online shop
item.description: What drives the price of a landing page, a company website and an online shop: design, content, CMS, payments, 1C sync and hosting.

item.title: Where AI actually lowers business costs, and where it doesn’t
item.description: The jobs where AI saves time and money: sorting requests, reading documents, drafting replies. And the jobs where it only adds cost and risk.

item.title: AI answering customers in Telegram: what to trust it with
item.description: An AI assistant can answer Telegram questions around the clock, but not all of them. How to set one up, when to hand over to a person, and what it costs.

item.title: AI for document processing: invoices, waybills and contracts
item.description: AI reads paper and PDF documents and enters the data into 1C or a spreadsheet, so nobody retypes it. Where it works and where a human check is a must.

item.title: App, website or Telegram Mini App: which one your business needs
item.description: How a mobile app, a website and a Telegram Mini App differ in cost, reach, payments and upkeep, and a simple way to choose for your own case.

item.title: MVP: what to leave out of the first version
item.description: The first version doesn’t need everything. How to choose MVP features, what to drop without regret, and how to know when it’s time for the next step.

item.title: UX mistakes that lose orders, from cart to payment
item.description: A customer adds to cart and leaves. The mistakes in websites, apps and bots that cost businesses orders, and how to find and fix them.

item.title: Designing for Uzbek and Russian speakers in one interface
item.description: Interfaces for a bilingual audience: choosing the language, Latin and Cyrillic, text length, the ʻ mark in fonts, dates and money formats.

item.title: Speed on a mid-range Android phone: why it costs you orders
item.description: Many customers open your site on a mid-range Android over mobile data, not a flagship on office Wi-Fi. How to test speed and what to fix first.

item.title: A chatbot customers don’t hate: design rules for Telegram bots
item.description: Endless menus, unwanted broadcasts, no way to reach a person. The mistakes that drive customers out of a bot, and practical rules for a usable one.

item.title: How to write a brief for an IT agency and get an accurate quote
item.description: A good brief makes the estimate sharper and the deadline more reliable. What to put on one or two pages: goal, users, features, limits, budget.

item.title: Hōrensō: how your software team should report to you
item.description: The Japanese practice of hōrensō: report, inform, consult. What to expect from a development team, how often and in what form, so there are no surprises.

item.title: Kaizen in software: why small improvements beat big releases
item.description: Launch is not the end of the project. How to improve a site, app or bot a little every month, how many hours to budget, and what to measure.

item.title: After launch: what maintaining an app or website actually involves
item.description: The app is live, but the work isn’t over. Updates, servers, security, store rules and small changes: what maintenance covers and how to budget for it.

item.title: Fixed price or hourly: how to set up a software development contract
item.description: The questions that matter in a development contract: payment model, stages, acceptance criteria, who owns the code and accounts, and the warranty.

item.title: Accepting Click, Payme and Uzum payments: a guide for business owners
item.description: How to add online payment to a website, app or Telegram bot: merchant agreements, the technical side, fiscal receipts, refunds and common mistakes.

item.title: Choosing a CRM: amoCRM, Bitrix24 or a custom system
item.description: amoCRM, Bitrix24 or a custom-built CRM: which fits your sales team, what to compare before choosing, and when building your own is worth it.

item.title: Connecting 1C to your site and Telegram bot: stock, prices, orders
item.description: Real stock on your site and no more retyping orders: how a 1C integration works and what to check before the work starts.

item.title: Storing personal data in Uzbekistan: sites, apps and bots
item.description: Personal data of Uzbek citizens must be stored on servers in the country. Here is what that means in practice for your website, app, bot and CRM.

item.title: Security for your site, app and bot: the minimum for a small business
item.description: Many problems start not with a clever attack but with a simple slip: a weak password, an open admin panel, an ex-employee’s login. What to check first.
